Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : BM6571 : Analytical Techniques in Bioengineering Laboratory { 0-0-3 / 2}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

At least 10 experiments from the following list of experiments will be carried out:
1. Analytical Bioengineering Foundations: Good Laboratory Practices, Quantitative Accuracy, Preparation of a 1 % (w/v) Sucrose Solution, and Introduction to Data Analysis and Statistical Interpretation of Data
2. Determination of Salicylic Acid Concentration by UV–Visible Spectroscopy
3. Measurement of Color Attributes by using a Reflective Colorimeter
4. Qualitative Evaluation of Color and Spectral Characteristics of Biomaterials Using Hyperspectral Imaging
5. Identification and Characterization of Functional Groups using ATR–FTIR Spectroscopy
6. Characterization of Electrical Characteristics of Biomaterials Using Electrical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS)
7. Assessment of the Viscoelastic Properties of Biomaterials Through Stress Relaxation Analysis Using a Texture Analyzer
8. Optical Characterization of Biomaterials Using Brightfield and Polarized Microscopy
9. Identification and Rf Analysis of Individual Components from a Mixed Dye Solution by Ascending and Circular Paper Chromatography
10. In-Vitro Evaluation of Tablet Disintegration Performance Using a Standard Disintegration Tester
11. In-Vitro Determination of Drug Release Behavior Using a Tablet Dissolution Apparatus
12. Quantitative Assessment of Sugar content by Refractometric Analysis
13. Optical Characterization of Emulgels using Fluorescence Microscopy
14. Study of Dehydration Kinetics of Biomaterials Using Empirical Mathematical Models
15. Measurement of Viscosity of Liquids using Ostwald Viscometer

Course Objective

1 .

The main objective of the course is to provide advanced hands-on training to students in the operation and application of modern analytical instruments used in bioengineering, enabling accurate quantitative and qualitative characterization of biomaterials and biological systems.
2 .

The course aims to develop strong competence in Good Laboratory Practices (GLP), experimental design, data acquisition, and statistical validation, ensuring accuracy, precision, reproducibility, and scientific integrity in analytical bioengineering experiments.
3 .

The course is designed to enhance students’ ability to interpret, analyze, and scientifically report experimental data using appropriate graphical, statistical, and analytical tools, thereby preparing them for research, industrial, and regulatory laboratory environments.

Course Outcome

1 .

Apply principles of GLP to ensure accuracy, precision, reproducibility, and safety in analytical experiments
2 .

Demonstrate hands-on proficiency in quantitative and qualitative analytical techniques
3 .

Perform data analysis and statistical interpretation to validate experimental outcomes
4 .

Integrate analytical bioengineering concepts using modern instrumentation
5 .

Develop the ability to interpret and report experimental results effectively with appropriate graphical, statistical, and scientific presentation skills following GLP and ethical standards

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : ID6173 : Design Practice { 0-0-3 / 2}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

General Lab Instructions and Environment Setup:
This module introduces students to the CATIA V6 interface and overall design environment. It covers essential lab practices, logging in, and setting up the project workspace to ensure a smooth start for CAD modeling activities.
Module 2 :

Sketcher Workbench:
Students learn how to invoke and use the Sketcher workbench to create precise 2D profiles and geometric shapes such as profiles, rectangles, circles, splines, ellipses, lines, axes, and points. The module also focuses on applying geometric constraints and transformation tools, followed by hands-on practice through a series of sketching exercises.
Module 3 :

Part Design Workbench:
This module focuses on transforming 2D sketches into 3D components. Students will create and modify solid features such as pads, pockets, shafts, grooves, holes, ribs, and slots. It also includes applying dress-up and transformation features like fillets, chamfers, shell, draft, patterns, mirrors, and Boolean operations.

Module 4 :

Assembly Design Workbench:
Students explore the creation of complex products by assembling multiple parts. The module covers building product structures, inserting and positioning components, and applying assembly constraints such as coincidence, contact, offset, and angle. Assembly operations like add, remove, and split are practiced through real-world examples including the Plummer Block, Knuckle Joint Assembly, and Screw Jack Assembly.
Module 5 :

Drafting Workbench:
This module teaches the generation of detailed 2D drawings from 3D models. Students learn to create various view types, including projection, section, detail, and clipping views. It also covers dimensioning, annotations, tables, and geometry modification tools. The module concludes with the generation of draft views from assembly models, reinforcing industry-standard documentation skills.
Module 6 :

Generative Shape Design Module:
The final module introduces advanced surface and hybrid modeling techniques. Students learn to create free-form and complex surfaces using the Generative Shape Design tools in CATIA V6, preparing them for high-level modeling tasks and specialized design challenges.

Course Objective

1 .

To familiarize students with the CATIA V6 interface and basic tools for 2D sketching, 3D modeling, and product design.
2 .

To enable students to create, assemble, and draft mechanical components and products.
3 .

To integrate digital modeling workflows with design intent, constraints, and engineering documentation.

Course Outcome

1 .

Use CATIA V6 for creating precise 2D sketches and complex 3D part models.
2 .

Assemble multiple components into functional products using assembly constraints.
3 .

Generate detailed engineering drawings and documentation from 3D models.

4 .

Develop surface and hybrid models using Generative Shape Design tools.
